newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end down in disinterested markets.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end down in disinterested markets.

text.p: Colombian stocks drifted down on continuing investor disinterest, brokers said.
Bogota's IBB index closed 0.05 percent down at 869.99 on a 1.3 billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended 0.13 percent lower at 13,585.07 on a thin 683 million peso trade.

"The exchanges are still showing the same trend of small volumes and minimal price fluctuation because there's little real sign of a drop in interest rates, which has caused traditional investors to be more cautious," one Bogota broker said.

Bogota's price index dipped slightly on the back of a wave of profit-taking in Banco de Colombia, down 2.09 percent at 420 on an 18 million peso trade, in Bancoquia, down 3.03 percent to 1,600 on a 8.95 million peso volume, and in Banco de Bogota, which ended 0.09 percent down at 6,005 on a 75 million peso trade.

The highlights of the session in Bogota were a deal in cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco, which ended 1.66 percent up at 3,050 on a 312 million peso volume, and a 310 million peso trade in insurance company Suramericana de Seguros, which remained unchanged at 18,500.

Bogota also saw demand for brewing giant Bavaria. Its share price nudged up 0.05 percent to 4,002 on a total trade of 265.8 million pesos. Cement manufacturer Cementos Diamante edged up 0.92 percent to 4,350, while Cementos Caribe closed 1.17 percent higher at 4,300.

"There was some underlying demand for these companies because good results are forecast, but it was being repressed by existing shareholders who were hoping to force prices up," another Bogota broker said. In Medellin, Banco de Colombia fell back 1.98 percent to 420.5 pesos on a 10 million peso volume and Banco Industrial de Colombia lost 0.42 percent, falling to 3,510.
